title: Past cricketers back  new Sri Lanka Cricket Bill | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 29 October 2026 03:46
-     - 16

Several veteran cricketers, through their lawyers, yesterday stated before the Supreme Court that “Sri Lankan cricket” should be freed from club administration, or from the politicised culture of cricket clubs.

The players also pointed out that, in order to further consolidate the achievements of cricketers both locally and internationally, an independent administrative unit should be established as stated in the draft.

The cricketers made these submissions while appearing as intervening petitioners in the petitions filed before the Supreme Court challenging the new Bill promulgated by the Government to govern, control, regulate, promote, and develop cricket in Sri Lanka.

These matters were presented by filing intervening petitions against six petitions filed by a group, including former Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) Head of Legal Affairs Attorney-at-Law Dr. Chanaka Senanayake, seeking an order declaring certain clauses of the Cricket Bill unconstitutional.

The Bill seeks to establish SLC to govern, control, regulate, promote, develop, and administer cricket in Sri Lanka; to promote the growth of cricket through the principles of good governance, integrity, transparency, accountability, inclusiveness, and equal opportunities; to protect the welfare of all participants and to protect cricket from corruption and other improper activities; and to provide for the establishment, powers, and functions of SLC and for matters connected therewith. The Bill was published in the Government Gazette on 28 September, and these intervention petitions were filed against the petitions stating that the provisions of the Bill, as published in the said Gazette, were unconstitutional.

The petitions were heard over three days before a three-judge bench comprising Supreme Court Justices Janak De Silva, Arjuna Obeyesekere, and Gihan Kulatunga.

Several veteran cricketers had filed intervening petitions in support of the Bill, and nine President’s Counsel appeared on behalf of the Test players, including Michael Tissera, Mahela Jayawardena, Rangana Herath, Champika Ramanayake, Roshan Mahanama, Kumar Sangakkara, and Sidath Wettimuny, and SLC Transformation Committee Chairman Eran Wickramaratne, on the advice of Sudath Perera Associates.

Presenting arguments in the petitions filed challenging the Bill, President’s Counsel Navin Marapana and other lawyers stated that certain clauses in the Bill are detrimental to the game of cricket.

He also pointed out that Section 32 of the proposed Bill provides that only “A” and “B” category sports clubs and provincial cricket associations are entitled to vote in SLC General Assembly meetings.

The proposed Bill will see a majority concentration of voting rights in the Western Province, while sports associations in other districts outside the Western Province will lose that right.

In addition, it was stated that the President is appointed the “Patron” of SLC through Section 28 of the relevant Bill, and that under Section 22, the Sports Ministry Secretary and the National Sports Council Chairman will be ex officio members of the board that will select independent directors for the Cricket Board.

The petitioners argued that such provisions undermine the independence of the SLC administration and violate the fundamental right to equality before the law guaranteed by Article 12(1) of the Constitution.

Accordingly, the petitioners have also requested the Supreme Court to rule that the relevant sections violate fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

On behalf of the intervenient petitioner cricketers, on the advice of Sudath Perera Associates, President’s Counsel Saliya Peiris, M.A. Sumanthiran, Ali Sabry, Uditha Egalahewa, Palitha Kumarasinghe, Faiszer Musthapha, Sanjeewa Jayawardena, Harsha Amarasekera, and Chandaka Jayasundara presented arguments in favour of the Bill, stating that the clauses of the Bill are constitutional.

They pointed out that this does not violate the Constitution and that Sri Lankan cricket should be taken out of the sports clubs. They pointed out that the administration of Sri Lankan cricket clubs is politicised and that sports club representatives are not acting for the betterment of cricket but as politicians with the aim of coming to power next.

Here, the Supreme Court judges asked the petitioners why such a law should be established by treating cricket as a separate sport. They also asked whether other sports in Sri Lanka are treated in this way.

The lawyers of the intervenient petitioners who responded stated that, considering the corruption and irregularities in cricket and the deteriorating state of the game in the country, it would be more appropriate to establish such an independent administrative unit. Since cricket has succeeded on the international stage compared to other sports, and attracts a large audience and circulates money, it is imperative to make it an independent unit, they said. 

After hearing the arguments of both sides for three days, the Supreme Court decided to forward its opinion to the Speaker.

President’s Counsel Navin Marapana, Kaushalya Navaratne, and Shiran Lakthilaka appeared on behalf of the petitioners.

Nine President’s Counsel appeared for the intervenient petitioners, as advised by Sudath Perera Associates.

Deputy Solicitor General Nirmalan Wigneswaran appeared on behalf of the Attorney General.

title: Fast bowling coach showers praise on Madushanka and Co. | Daily FT
summary:

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Sri Lanka will prime up for Saturday’s final against Pakistan when they take on England in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore today in a game which will not have any bearing on the standings. It is the final match of the league round.

Sri Lanka’s emphatic eight-wicket win over the host country Pakistan on Tuesday has resulted in this match being reduced to a dead rubber. England, without a win after three matches – losing the last two of them after being in winning positions, will try to return home at least with a consolation win.

Following their loss to Pakistan in the curtain-raiser match of the Tri-Series, Sri Lanka has fought back magnificently to be within touching distance of laying their hands on a silverware, after back-to-back wins against England and Pakistan.

If the win against England was orchestrated by their batsmen who chased down a record score of 430, victory against Pakistan belonged to their bowlers who ran through the host’s batting for 110.

Spearheading the bowling was left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka who finished with career best figures of 5/34.  

Sri Lanka’s fast bowling coach South African-born Ryan van Niekerk was all-excited about the progress Madushanka has made as a fast bowler in white ball cricket.

“Dilshan is a highly talented young bowler. He has all the skill sets, he swings the ball and he’s got a great bouncer. That’s been a big part of his progression in how to use his aggressive deliveries to make his other deliveries more of a weapon,” said van Niekerk.

“It’s just hoping how our bowlers understand their wicket taking deliveries and when to use them. You saw tonight when he bowls his bouncer really well, it makes his front foot ball really dangerous. At the moment he is getting wickets with his bouncer but he is able to swing the ball and he is really accurate.”

“We only bowled one wide in 25 overs today as a group of bowlers. That discipline mixed with aggression and a wicket-taking mentality has certainly helped him and continues to develop. He is eager to bowl. He wants to bowl all the time so I had to get him to slow down a little bit with his loads, but in general love the way he has progressed.”

Van Niekerk said that the three fast bowlers Madushanka, Eshan Malinga and Asitha Fernando complimented each other really well in the game against Pakistan.

“Eshan got a four-fer in the first game in that losing cause. I think there is great development as a fast bowling group and it was capped off nicely by Dilshan. We had to bounce back. It wasn’t too long ago the same bowling unit went for 430,” pointed out Van Nierkerk.

“From our point of view, bowling with a different intentionality, mentality around taking wickets, and looking to be positive and aggressive around our bowling and, on top of that, just an execution process. A lot of the time we got good plans but not being able to execute them more consistently. When we are all taking wickets a little bit more regularly it does help with the momentum of the game. Our bowling group as a whole capitalized on that momentum and I thought the execution was up there.”

Speaking on the Tri-Series in its entirety, van Niekerk said, “If you’ve watched anything in this tournament so far it has been unbelievable cricket throughout. I wouldn’t worry about a shortened match like this. The cricket that’s been played and what’s been on offer in all the matches, I think fans would be crazy not to come in and celebrate at the grounds. Good cricket wickets and three good teams.”

Sri Lanka are likely to test their bench strength and may rest a few key players and give those who have not had a game in the Tri-Series so far an opportunity today. Kamil Mishara, Lahiru Udara, Dushmantha Chameera and Maheesh Theekshana have not played a single match, while Sachindu Colombage played only in the opening game against Pakistan.

Managed by Aitken Spence Hotels, the hospitality arm of Aitken Spence PLC, The Rainforest Ecolodge is entering a new chapter, placing the Sinharaja Forest Reserve, its biodiversity, and the communities living alongside it at the heart of the guest experience. 

This renewed direction strengthens the property’s role as the hospitality gateway to one of Sri Lanka’s most significant natural landscapes, bringing together responsible hospitality, conservation, and the spirit of discovery.

Set within the Enselwatte Tea Estate and adjoining the Sinharaja Forest Reserve, the ecolodge occupies one of Sri Lanka’s most extraordinary natural settings and holds a LEED® Platinum certification from the US Green Building Council, reflecting the principles of sustainability embedded in its design and construction. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Man and the Biosphere Reserve, the Sinharaja is Sri Lanka’s last viable area of primary tropical rainforest, supporting an exceptional concentration of endemic plants, birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, invertebrates, and aquatic life.

The relaunch positions The Rainforest Ecolodge as the hospitality gateway to this living ecosystem: a place for travellers who want to do more than simply stay near nature. It is designed for those who want to enter the forest with curiosity, understand what they encounter, immerse themselves in the rainforest, and leave with a stronger connection to the natural world and self.”

Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC Chairperson Stasshani Jayawardena said: “The Rainforest Ecolodge gives us an opportunity to bring people closer to one of Sri Lanka’s most remarkable natural treasures, while ensuring that conservation and local communities remain an integral part of that experience. I strongly believe that’s how we create meaningful travel experiences. This is very much in keeping with how we, at Aitken Spence, see the future of tourism; thoughtful, responsible, and deeply connected to place.”

Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC Managing Director Susith Jayawickrama said: “Our vision for The Rainforest Ecolodge is to create a deeper relationship between hospitality, conservation and discovery. The Sinharaja is an extraordinary natural asset, and our responsibility is to ensure that every guest experience contributes to a greater understanding and appreciation of this remarkable landscape, while supporting the communities that live alongside it. We want the ecolodge to be more than just a place to stay; we want it to become a meaningful gateway to understanding one of Sri Lanka’s most vital and vibrant ecosystems.”

The ecolodge’s approach has received recognition across sustainability and hospitality platforms. In 2026, The Rainforest Ecolodge was named Silver Winner in the ‘Nature Positive’ category at the ICRT Indian Subcontinent Awards, recognising its work in biodiversity conservation, responsible nature-based experiences, community benefit, and conservation education. It was also named Sri Lanka’s Leading Lodge 2026 at the World Travel Awards, reinforcing its position as one of the country’s most distinctive nature-led stays.

Recognised as Sri Lanka’s first officially classified ecolodge by the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority, the property was conceived around responsible tourism from the beginning. Its 20 chalets were created using repurposed shipping containers and other recycled materials, allowing the accommodation to sit lightly within the surrounding tea estate at the forest’s edge. Private decks, modern amenities and immersive views offer comfort without separating guests from the landscape.

Yet the true experience begins beyond the chalet.

Early mornings unfold to a chorus of birdsong, with guided birdwatching walks offering glimpses of mixed-species flocks moving through the canopy and endemic birds appearing in flashes of colour. Daytime trails introduce guests to the layered structure of the rainforest, its medicinal plants and diverse wildlife, while waterfall journeys lead through forested paths to clear streams and natural pools. Night walks reveal an entirely different ecosystem shaped by frog calls, moths, geckos, bats, and other nocturnal life.

The lodge’s location at the meeting point of dense rainforest and cultivated tea land creates a distinctive ecological transition zone, offering naturalists, photographers, and citizen scientists, opportunities to observe how wildlife moves between different habitats.

The property’s developing Nature Interpretation Centre and Online Knowledge Hub will bring together information, publications, audiovisual material, species profiles, conservation insights, and field notes related to the Sinharaja. They are intended to serve travellers, students, citizen scientists, and nature enthusiasts before, during, and after their stay, transforming the ecolodge into a growing repository of rainforest knowledge.

Future collaborations with conservation organisations, universities, naturalists, wildlife photographers, artists, wellness practitioners, and biodiversity experts, will broaden the scope and deepen the impact of this initiative. The ambition is to support citizen science efforts, observations, and acoustic indulgences, conservation storytelling and responsible access to the rainforest, while creating a facilitation platform through which experts and enthusiasts can share their findings with a wider audience.

Community remains central to this model. Local employment, naturalist-led experiences, productive community relations and engagement, rural knowledge, food traditions, and livelihoods all connect the guest experience to the surrounding region. From ‘kithul’ tapping and medicinal plant knowledge to tea cultivation and village life, the rainforest story is inseparable from the people who have lived and worked beside it for generations.

This is where regenerative tourism becomes more than an idea. Guests are invited to experience the Sinharaja with care, support local livelihoods, and understand how conservation benefits both ecosystems and communities. The aim is not simply to reduce impact, but to build a tourism model that contributes meaningfully to the long-term ecological and social health of the locality.

For the conscious explorer, The Rainforest Ecolodge offers a rare kind of escape. It is a place to disconnect from noise, reconnect with nature, pursue a lifelong interest in wildlife, or begin learning about biodiversity for the first time. It can be a retreat for birdwatchers, photographers, artists, and nature lovers, or simply a quiet space for travellers seeking stillness, fresh air, and a deeper sense of place.

Lanka Pass is being built to bring more of these businesses together in one platform and make them easier for travellers to discover.

The platform also aims to go beyond a traditional collection of tours and excursions. Alongside curated experiences, Lanka Pass will bring together savings, exclusive discounts and additional benefits, as well as useful travel content including guides and audio guides, giving travellers more value throughout their journey.

Importantly, Lanka Pass is proudly built and operated in Sri Lanka, with its technology, operations and partnerships managed locally. The platform is being developed with a strong focus on connecting international travellers with Sri Lankan businesses and experiences, while helping more local operators benefit from the country’s growing tourism industry.

Lanka Pass Founder Kasun Perera said: “Lanka Pass came from seeing an opportunity to better connect travellers with the local tourism ecosystem by experiencing similar platforms in Europe and the US. There are so many incredible businesses and experiences across Sri Lanka, and we wanted to create a platform that makes them easier to discover while also giving local operators an opportunity to reach more travellers.”

Perera is a CIMA-qualified finance and analytics professional who has worked across Sri Lanka and the UK and currently works in London in a leading investment bank. 

His experience abroad helped shape the idea for Lanka Pass and the opportunity to create a more connected way for international travellers to experience Sri Lanka.

As the platform prepares for launch, Lanka Pass is currently building its first group of local experience providers and tourism partners across the island.

The aim is simple: to make discovering Sri Lanka easier and more rewarding for travellers, while helping more of the local businesses behind those experiences benefit from the country’s growing international tourism industry.

It also achieved a room acquisition cost equivalent to just 6.7% of the room cost, compared with the industry benchmark cited for online travel agency (OTA) bookings of approx. 20%.
